answer: Submissions that land within 271 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The zenith detector writes to voyage, and summit publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 147 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
